title: Red Team Diversity Requirements for Comprehensive Coverage

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible chain from red team diversity to coverage comprehensiveness. Gap: analyzing published reports for diversity is observational, and data on team composition may be incomplete or unavailable.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Literature analysis and quantitative comparison of published red team reports is accessible with standard research tools and no ML expertise required.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Systematically accessing and analyzing published red team reports requires sustained literature review, and connecting team composition to coverage variance requires data that may be incomplete.

novelty.reasoning: Red team diversity is discussed qualitatively -- the IMDA Singapore AI Safety Red Teaming Challenge covers multilingual/multicultural dimensions, and guidelines recommend diverse teams. The 'Can We Trust AI Benchmarks?' review (AIES 2025, DOI 10.1609/aies.v8i1.36595) flags demographic and cultural skews. Automatic red-team pipelines improve attack diversity. However, no quantitative study exists that analyzes published red team reports for team composition diversity and correlates it with coverage variance. The quantitative analysis of diversity-coverage correlation is mostly novel.
